newsitem.title: INDIA: India BPL Cellular Holdings postpones ADR pricing.
newsitem.headline: India BPL Cellular Holdings postpones ADR pricing.

text.p: Indian telecom firm BPL Cellular Holdings has postponed the pricing of its issue of American Depositary Recepits (ADR), a spokesman for lead manager Morgan Stanley said on Friday.
"The pricing is likely to take place on Monday in order to meet investor demand for one-on-one meetings with the compnay," the spokesman told Reuters.
The ADR issue --- India's first -- was scheduled to be priced on November 21 in the U.S.
Investment bankers said negative publicity ahead of the pricing of the $185 million issue had made investors jittery.
They said investors were seeking clarifications on an auditors report by KPMG Peat Marwick which is included in the ADR prospectus.

"...The company's significant working capital deficiency, significant operating losses incurred during the build-out phase of its digital mobile and radio paging networks, net capital deficiency and significant capital needs for the continued build-out of these networks raise substantial doubt about its ability to continue as a growing concern," the auditor's report said.

A note to the firm's consolidated financial statements says the BPL Cellular is still in the system build-out phase of its digital mobile and radio paging networks and has consequently incurred significant operating losses from its inception through March 31, 1996.
It says the company has a working capital deficiency of 2,194 million rupees and a net capital deficiency of 3,558 million.
"To date, the company has been dependent on financing received from the BPL Group and its affiliates, minority shareholders of its subsidiaries and from financial institutions," the note says.

It points out that the management's plans for future financing depends primarily on this initial offering of shares in the United States and additional debt financing likely to be arranged after the ADR.

"Although management believes such sources of financing will be adequate to meet the company's cash requirements in the next 12-18 months, there are no assurances that such financings, none of which have been finalised, can be successfully completed within that timeframe," the note says.
BPL Cellular is one of three fledgling Indian telecom firm which have decided to tap the U.S. market for funds. Bharati Televentures and Hutchison Max are also planning ADR issues.
